name: Workshop Summary Report
obj: Turn workshop outputs into a concise synthesis of what was explored, created and decided, with next steps.
when: Within 5 working days of the workshop.
inputs: Photos, Miro boards, idea sheets, notes.
output: Summary report: ambition, discussions, insights, ideas, priorities, decisions, open questions, action plan.
std: Page 1 answers 'what did we decide, who does what, by when'; discussion vs decision vs to-validate visibly separated.
quality: Concise, visual, decision-oriented, readable by non-attendees.
mistakes: A photo dump · decisions not marked · no owners.
example: HEAL: page 1 — Decided: test protected mealtimes on Ward 4 (owner: ward manager, by 15 Jan) · To validate: same-day ordering with dietitians · Discussed: family updates (privacy review). [fictional]

var.PLAY: To validate: lockers with safety officer.

prompt: 'From these workshop outputs [paste], draft a summary: page 1 = Decided / To validate / Discussed with owners and dates (leave [TBC] where unknown). Do not invent decisions.'
verify: Every 'Decided' item was decided in the room; owners confirmed.
l_obj: Write a first page that separates decisions, validations and discussions with owners.
explain: Don't report the workshop. Translate it into action.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: Two days later, a sponsor who missed it asks 'so what did we decide?'
questions: How do you separate discussion, decision, to-validate?

answer_key.sample_answer: Three labelled blocks with owner and date; actions have verbs and deadlines.
answer_key.success_criteria: Three categories visible; every action has owner + date or TBC.

name: Prioritising Ideas Workshop
obj: Decide which ideas move forward using agreed criteria: user value, impact, feasibility, strategic fit.
who: Facilitator runs · Client decision-makers decide · Operations and tech assess feasibility.
acc: Client sponsor owns decisions; facilitator owns the process.
when: After the summary, with decision-makers present.
steps: Identify quick wins and strategic bets
output: Prioritised portfolio: move forward, test, combine, refine, postpone or stop — with rationale.
std: Criteria agreed before scoring; rationale written for each decision.
quality: Not voting alone; desirability visible next to feasibility.
mistakes: Dot-vote only · criteria after the vote · no owners.
example: WORK: team-table = quick win (standard offer, adapted); anchor-day planner = strategic bet (needs app capability); quiet zone = test.

var.PLAY: Family bundle quick win; lockers strategic bet.
var.HEAL: Protected mealtimes quick win; same-day ordering bet pending clinical review.

prompt: 'Score these ideas [table] against criteria [list with weights]. Show the score breakdown and the 3 biggest uncertainties per idea. Do not decide.'
verify: Scores reflect the group's judgement; AI scores are a discussion aid only.
fallback: Impact/effort 2x2 on the wall with agreed definitions.
l_obj: Handle a popular-but-infeasible idea without dismissing the group, using pre-agreed criteria.
explain: Prioritisation is not voting. It is collective decision-making.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: The group dot-votes; the most popular idea is the least feasible.
questions: Which criteria should have been agreed first?
Quick win vs strategic bet vs parked idea?

answer_key.sample_answer: Acknowledge the desirability signal; ask what would make it feasible; classify as strategic bet with a test. Criteria: user value, feasibility, cost, strategic fit.
answer_key.success_criteria: Criteria named and weighted before scoring.

name: Value Proposition Workshop
obj: Clarify the value of each selected concept for users, the client and Sodexo before further investment.
who: Facilitator runs · Client and account team contribute business value.
acc: CoDesign lead; account owner for business value.
output: Value proposition per concept: target, need, experience, benefits, differentiation, business value, assumptions to test.
std: Written as benefits, not features; assumptions listed for 06.X3.
example: PLAY: 'Family bundle: parents get the kids fed before the whistle with one tap, so the family watches the second half together.' Assumption: families will buy before match day.

var.WORK: Team table: 'lunch becomes the team meeting, in 20 minutes'.
var.HEAL: Protected mealtimes: 'patients eat with help at the right time'.
var.LEARN: Commuter bundle: 'a predictable price for a whole campus day'.

prompt: 'For concept [x] and persona [y], write the value proposition as benefits, list differentiation and the 3 assumptions to test first. No figures unless supplied.'
fallback: Canvas: Target → Jobs → Pains → Gains → Concept → Benefits → Assumptions.
l_obj: Rewrite a feature-led concept into a benefit for a named user and pick the first assumption to test.
explain: Don't describe what the concept does. Explain why it matters.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: A concept reads 'a digital platform that centralises all services'.

answer_key.sample_answer: 'For the team lead organising an office day, book room, table and lunch in one step.' Test: will team leads plan the day before? 2-week trial.
answer_key.success_criteria: Benefit names user and job; test is concrete.

name: Annexes
obj: Package the evidence behind the deliverable so it is traceable, safe to share and reusable.
std: Each key finding links to its evidence ID; personal data removed.
mistakes: Dumping 400 photos · names in transcripts · no index.
handoff: Repository filed in SharePoint; feeds 06.X6 credential.
example: LEARN: index by phase; finding 'the gap is the valley' links to interviews St04, St11 and timetable analysis. [fictional]
prompt: Generic Claude prompt: 'Propose an index for these files [list] by phase and topic, and flag files likely to contain personal data.'
l_obj: Decide what goes in the annex and make one finding traceable.
explain: Keep the main story simple. Keep the evidence accessible.

questions: What goes in, what stays out?
How do you make a finding traceable?
What do you remove or anonymise?

answer_key.sample_answer: Selected, indexed evidence; evidence IDs on findings; remove names, faces, health data.

name: Concept Development (post-workshop)
obj: Strengthen the ideas selected in prioritisation into robust concepts, combining participants' idea sheets with evidence and constraints.
who: CoDesign team develops · Operations, tech, dietitians or safety as relevant review.
inputs: Selected idea sheets, value propositions, constraints.
steps: Detail the service blueprint (front and back stage)
output: Developed concept + service blueprint + assumption list.
std: Every component has an owner hypothesis; assumptions ranked.
quality: Faithful to participants' intent; operationally credible.
mistakes: Replacing participant ideas with the team's favourite.
example: WORK: Team Table merges 3 idea sheets; blueprint shows booking, kitchen batch timing and table signage.

var.HEAL: Same-day choice incl. diet check step.

prompt: 'Merge these idea sheets [paste] into one concept, keeping participants' wording; add a front/back-stage blueprint and dependencies.'
fallback: Blueprint on Miro: user actions / frontline / back stage / systems.
l_obj: Merge idea sheets into a concept with a blueprint and ranked assumptions.
explain: Workshop ideas become concepts only after evidence and operations have had their say.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: Three idea sheets overlap on 'team lunch'.
questions: What do you keep from each?
What does the back stage need?

answer_key.sample_answer: Keep each sheet's user benefit; back stage needs kitchen batch timing; riskiest: teams commit the day before.

name: Solution & Capability Mapping (Spark / Standard Offer)
sub: PROPOSED EXTENSION · from need to capability
obj: Start from the user and operational capability each concept needs, then check product fit, availability, dependencies and ownership.
acc: Tech owner validates fit; CoDesign lead keeps the user need visible.
when: After concept development, before pilot design.
inputs: Developed concepts, Standard Offer and Innovation Catalogue.
steps: Write the required capability in user terms
output: Capability map per concept: capability → candidate solution → status → owner → validation needed.
std: Capability written before product; every 'standard' item still has a validation note.
mistakes: Starting from the catalogue · assuming standard means validated · forcing exact 70/20/10 ratios.
example: HEAL: 'choose closer to the meal' needs bedside ordering + diet check; candidate: existing ordering tablet (adapted standard), dependency: diet data feed (owner TBC).

var.WORK: Team booking: workplace app (standard) + group pre-order (adapted).

prompt: Solution Intelligence Engine: 'Map these prioritised concepts [paste] to Standard Offer and Innovation Catalogue; for each, capability needed, candidate, availability, dependencies, owner [TBC if unknown].'
verify: Availability and ownership with the tech owner; no capability claimed without confirmation.
fallback: Table: Capability / Candidate / Standard-Adapted-Innovation / Status / Owner / Validation.
l_obj: Write a capability before naming a product and classify it with the 70/20/10 lens.
explain: Start with what the user and operation need. Then find what we have.

exercise.situation: A concept needs 'families notified when the patient has eaten'.

answer_key.sample_answer: Capability: 'confirmed meal status shared with consented family'. Likely innovation/pilot. Validate privacy, consent, nurse workload.

name: Prototype & User Test
obj: Test the riskiest assumptions with real users using the cheapest prototype that can answer the question.
who: CoDesign team designs the test · Site team hosts · Users take part.
acc: CoDesign lead; site manager approves on-site tests.
steps: Write the test question and success signal
output: Test plan + results: assumption, method, participants, signal, result, decision.
mistakes: Asking 'would you use this?' · testing everything at once.
handoff: Tested concepts → 06.X4. Tested concepts require user evidence; benchmark and AI ideas do not count as validation.
example: PLAY: paper menu + mock locker at one gate for one match; signal: 30% of families in that stand pre-order.

var.HEAL: Tablet mock-up with 5 patients, nurse present.

deck: Proposed · [S06, slides 5-6] Labs 'Garage: prototype, test, learn'
prompt: Generic Claude prompt: 'For assumption [x], propose 3 low-cost tests with method, participants, success signal and risks.'
fallback: Assumption / Test / Signal / Result / Decision table.
l_obj: Turn an assumption into a test with a pre-defined success signal.
explain: Test the riskiest thing first, as cheaply as possible.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: Assumption: families will pre-order before match day.
questions: What would make you drop it?

answer_key.sample_answer: Offer the bundle on the ticket page for one match; signal ≥ X% (agreed beforehand); drop if near zero after 2 matches.

name: Pilot Design, Business Case & Measures
sub: PROPOSED EXTENSION · prove it in operation
obj: Design a time-boxed pilot with baseline, measures, costs and decision rules.
acc: Client sponsor and account owner approve the pilot.
inputs: Tested concept, capability map, baseline data.
steps: Estimate costs and benefits with sources
output: Pilot plan + measurement plan + draft business case.
std: Baseline exists; no benefit figure without a source or 'to measure'.
mistakes: Pilot with no baseline · invented ROI.
example: LEARN: one-semester commuter bundle pilot; measures: uptake, dwell time, affordability perception vs baseline survey; decision rule agreed with dining director.
deck: Proposed · [S06, slide 4] 'pilot KPIs against a baseline'
prompt: Impact Map agent: 'Build an impact map for pilot [x]: activities → outputs → outcomes → measures, marking which measures have a baseline.'
verify: Every figure sourced or marked 'to measure'.
fallback: Pilot canvas: Scope / Baseline / Measures / Cost / Decision rule / Owner.
l_obj: Write a pilot decision rule with a baseline and 3 measures.
explain: A pilot without a baseline proves nothing.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: The sponsor wants 'to see if it works'.

answer_key.sample_answer: Experience, operational and cost measures; baseline from pre-pilot weeks; rule: scale if ≥ agreed threshold on 2 of 3.

name: Roadmap & Implementation Handover
obj: Sequence initiatives into a roadmap and hand them over to the people who will run them, with decisions, owners, assumptions and measures.
acc: Account owner owns the roadmap after handover.
when: Final phase; then reviewed in QBRs (quarterly business reviews).
steps: Write the handover note: decisions, assumptions, measures, risks
output: Roadmap + handover note + final restitution deck.
std: Each initiative: owner, date, measure, open assumption.
mistakes: Roadmap without owners · handover by email only.
handoff: Owners accept in writing; first review date set.
example: WORK: Now team-table (floor 6 → all floors), Next anchor-day planner (app capability), Later quiet zones; owners named; review at next QBR.
cred: Eli Lilly 5-year roadmap cited in S05 slide 25 — confirm artifact.
prompt: 'Build a Now/Next/Later roadmap from these initiatives [table] with owner, dependency, measure, open assumption; mark unknown owners [TBC].'
verify: Owners and dates confirmed by people, not inferred.
l_obj: Produce a handover note that names decisions, owners, assumptions and measures.
explain: A roadmap nobody owns is a poster.

templates.label: Project template root (SharePoint) — specific template: TO LOCATE, owner Gabriel

exercise.situation: The project ends Friday; the account manager inherits 5 initiatives.
questions: What goes in the handover note?

answer_key.sample_answer: Decisions, owners, assumptions, measures, risks; account owner signs; first review at next QBR.

name: Credential Capture
sub: PROPOSED EXTENSION · make the proof reusable
obj: Capture an approved credential the week after close-out, stating what it actually demonstrates.
who: CoDesign team drafts · Account owner and client approve.
when: Week after close-out; update after pilot results.
steps: State what it proves and what it does not
std: Each claim has a source; sharing level stated (internal / client-shareable / public).
mistakes: Claiming impact before measurement · no approval.
example: HEAL: 'St Aldric meal journey: method and pilot design. Impact: to be measured (pilot ends Feb).' [fictional]
prompt: Credential Writer: 'From this restitution [paste], draft a credential card; mark every unmeasured outcome as "to be measured".'
fallback: Template: Client context → Challenge → Approach → Outputs → Results (measured) → What it proves.
l_obj: Write a credential that separates delivered outputs from measured impact.
explain: A credential listing proves we did the project, not that it worked.

exercise.situation: The project just closed; results are not measured yet.

answer_key.sample_answer: Claim approach and outputs; impact waits for measurement; account owner + client approve.
